_comment: Fixed lines the assistant speaks without the language model, from docs/call-flow.md and docs/memory.md (variant B, dial-in). Keyed by Gnani locale code; a code with no entry uses the entry with the same language prefix, then en-IN (logged). No line tells the caller about memory or forget me; whether to remember a call is asked at its end. howCanIHelp follows the language confirmation for a new or withheld caller so the line is never silent. Every language in g-one.languages has an entry (FixedLinesCoverageTest). welcome is spoken only on a call that starts in a fixed language; after the English-first language question it is skipped, because the opener already introduced G-One. {name} is the name the farmer gave on an earlier call. The assistant voice is female, so Hindi lines use feminine verb forms. No digits: Timbre reads numbers better as words. askEnd, askSave and carryOn are the end-of-call check (agent/closing): asked of every party still on the call, each answered with yes or no; askSave says main points, never a recording. The ask* lines answer a party who speaks to G-One directly during mediation (agent/mediation/AskLines): every answer is one or more of these lines with typed facts filled in as words, never free text from a model. askValue and askPerKg are G-One's own calculation and say so. askNoLimits is a buyer asking what the farmer would accept, their limits or for negotiation advice, answered without the model.
_review: The ta-IN, kn-IN, bn-IN and bn-en lines (and their welcomeBack and howCanIHelp, askEnd, askSave and carryOn lines) are machine-authored and have not been checked by a native speaker. They need native-speaker review before a demo. Hinglish and Benglish are written in the native script with English words, as in local-replies.json. All ask* lines in ta-IN, kn-IN, bn-IN, bn-en and hi-en are machine-authored too and need the same review.
